predecessors.name: Lucanians
predecessors.text: 'almost the entire current province of Cosenza', northern boundary 'from the river Laus ... to the Crathis'; capital Consentia

successors.name: Roman Republic
successors.text: the Bruttian country that 'corresponds approximately to modern Calabria' without its southern tip: the Cosenza, Catanzaro and Vibo Valentia provinces, with Hipponium, Terina and Thurii once occupied

ledger.x: c. 356 BC: the Bruttii rise from the Lucanians. 'The rise of the Bruttii is dated by ancient authors to approximately 356 BC', 'Their independence seems to have been readily acknowledged by the Lucanians'; they 'coalesced into a league, the Confoederatio Bruttiorum', capital Consentia.
Before 334 BC: the Bruttians occupy Hipponium, Terina and Thurii 'less than 30 years after their first revolt' (undated).
331 BC: Alexander of Epirus dies at Pandosia, 'killed by a Lucanian'; the page is silent on what became of his Italian holdings, so the return of Terina is a bridge.
282 BC: the Bruttians join the war on Rome.

c. 272 BC: the Bruttii make peace. 'The years after 275 saw renewed Roman campaigns against the three tribes' (Samnites, Lucanians, Bruttians); Tarentum fell in 272. The Bruttii page: 'subdued by Fabricius and Papirius' and 'compelled to purchase peace by the surrender of one-half of the great forest of Sila'. No page…

203 BC: Rome 'dissolved the Confederation, took away Consentia's city-state status, and confiscated most of the land as ager publicus'; the cities were 'called allies but forbidden to make alliances on their own and to mint coins', and the Bruttians were 'deprived of the right to bear arms'.
203 BC: the Confederation of the Bruttii is dissolved after Hannibal's departure; Rome founds colonies at Tempsa, Crotona, Vibo Valentia and Thurii (undated).

wars.name: Italian campaign of Alexander I of Epirus
wars.outcome: Alexander took Heraclea from the Lucanians and Terina from the Bruttii, made a treaty with Rome (332) and was killed at Pandosia (331 on his page, 326 on the Bruttii page); his Italian conquests were not kept.

wars.name: Pyrrhic War
wars.outcome: Roman victory: Pyrrhus left Italy in 275, Tarentum fell in 272, and the Bruttii, who 'bore the full brunt of the war', were subdued and bought peace with half of the Sila forest.

wars.name: Second Punic War
wars.outcome: Bruttium, allied with Hannibal after Cannae, was a Carthaginian base from 215; Hannibal withdrew to it in 207 and fought at Crotona in 204; the Romans retook it in 204-202 and dissolved the Bruttian League.

certainty.note: Only the northern line (Laus to Crathis) and the coasts are given; no treaty line.
